messages:
anya: FYI seeing a sustained saturation event in the EU dedicated pool (eu-west-1). p95 token latency jump across several hosts, some tenants approaching SLA thresholds. possible noisy neighbor + KV cache thrash. :rotating_light:
chris: link to dashboards? which pool id?
anya: pool=dedicated-eu-42. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/pool/dedicated-eu-42?from=now-1h to=now
dave: grabbing profilers. initial read: kernel_selector fallback spikes and kv_cache_eviction_rate increases at the same time as queue length.
chris: can you paste the profiler snippet here?
anya: pasted small snippet from runtime trace:
```
[2026-06-01T14:00:12Z] host=gpu-eu-42-7 kernel_selector: fallback_count=187 -> generic_attn_kernel (slow path)
[2026-06-01T14:00:13Z] host=gpu-eu-42-7 kv_cache: evictions=312 miss_rate=0.48 prefix_cache_size_mb=24
[2026-06-01T14:00:13Z] host=gpu-eu-42-7 batcher: avg_batch_ms=52 queue_len=18
```
anya: p95 token latency went from ~85ms -> ~410ms over 10m window. throughput down ~22%.
elainE (ELAINE): (note: use all lowercase display) we have a heavy tenant (acme-corp) running high-seq long-context reranks on that pool since 13:40 UTC. looks correlated.
chris: noisy neighbor indeed. why are kernels falling back? should be using opt kernels for the model.
dave: preliminary hypothesis: when evictions spike KV cache misses increase token recompute leading to longer seqs; runtime falls back to generic kernel if mem pressure changes or if sequence length distribution shifts unexpectedly. kernel selection logic currently prefers specialized kernels when < max_seq, but eviction can shrink available workspace mid-request and trigger fallback.
anya: also seeing an uptick in device SM utilization variance on host gpu-eu-42-7, host shows hot loops from long-running sessions.
oncall-bot: incident-1882345600 created by anya at 2026-06-01T14:00:00Z, severity=sev2, assigned=eng-runtime oncall
chris: mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily throttle acme-corp job (rate-limit tokens or throttle concurrency). 2) move high-seq reranks off the dedicated-eu-42 pool to another pool with spare capacity. 3) force runtime to prefer the safe kernel even if slower — avoids mid-request fallback churn.
sam: we can add placement affinity to avoid mixing long-seq jobs with low-latency tenants in a pool. but moving jobs takes ~2-3min to drain.
anya: doing step 1 now: applying soft quota to tenant acme-corp in placement manager. command:
```bash
placementctl set-quota --tenant acme-corp --pool dedicated-eu-42 --qps 30 --reason "incident mitigation"
```
chris: nice. can we also temporarily bump kv prefix cache size for that pool? might reduce evictions.
dave: prefix_cache is per-host and currently at 24MB. we can increment to 64MB but need to watch memory fragmentation on GPUs. willing to try on a subset of hosts.
anya: rolling apply to 3 hosts now: gpu-eu-42-{3,7,9}.
chris: after quota applied p95 dropped from 410ms -> 210ms within 90s, throughput recovered ~12%. good sign.
dave: kernel_selector fallback_count on those hosts also dropped by ~80%. kv_evictions down to ~40/min.
elainE: customer success pinged acme-corp to ask if they can shift batch windows. they're open to short throttle for now.
oncall-bot: deploy activity: placementctl change applied by anya at 2026-06-01T14:05:30Z
chris: next steps I propose:
- short term (now): keep soft quota for 30m, continue rolling prefix cache increase on two more hosts.
- medium term (24-72h): tweak kernel selection to avoid mid-request fallback: add safety check to reserve workspace estimate before choosing specialized kernel. add metric kernel_workspace_reserve_failures.
- longer term: improve scheduler to surface long-seq heavy tenants and enforce placement policies to avoid mixing. also consider tenant isolation knobs (dedicated-shares).
dave: added two TODOs to runtime repo and created a minimal repro harness to reproduce eviction->fallback sequence. PR will include additional logging.
anya: action items:
- anya: keep quota + monitor (30m)
- dave: land prefix_cache rollout + open PR for safer kernel selection (ETA 48h)
- chris: draft placement policy change and add alert for kv_eviction_rate > 0.3 on dedicated pools
- sam: prepare migration plan for moving long-seq tenants out of hot pools
- elaine: coordinate with CS on customer communication
chris: marking incident as mitigated for now but not closed. will keep on watch for 2h. :white_check_mark:
anya: thanks all — posting follow-up when PRs are up or if metrics regress.
chris: QA note for postmortem: include exact sequence lengths and model variants that trigger fallback, and attach perf profiles for before/after prefix_cache bump.
anya: acknowledged.
